graph_meta.problem_text: A piggy bank contains hundred 50p coins, fifty ₹1 coins, twenty ₹2 coins and ten ₹5 coins. If it is equally likely that one of the coins will fall out when the bank is turned upside down, what is the probability that the coin (i) will be a 50p coin? (ii) will not be a ₹5 coin?
graph_meta.sympy_note: There is no unknown, so there is no equation: SymPy and the claim checker check the numeric lines (100 + 50 + 20 + 10 = 180, 100/180 = 5/9, 170/180 = 17/18, 1 − 1/18 = 17/18).
graph_meta.guided_note: Guided mode (Q10 hint sheet): one question at a time; a wrong answer shows Hint 1, then 2, then 3. Q3 (total) and Q4 (part i) are shared; at method_choice the student answers either path's first question, and Jev picks which path's hints to show for a wrong answer.
graph_meta.description: Guided solution DAG for NCERT Class 10 Ex 14.1 Q10 (piggy bank: 100 × 50p, 50 × ₹1, 20 × ₹2, 10 × ₹5; answers (i) 5/9 (ii) 17/18). Shared: total 180 and part (i) 100/180 = 5/9. Part (ii): Path A counts the coins that are not ₹5 (170/180); Path B uses the complement rule (1 − 10/180).

problem_context.source: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 14 Probability, Exercise 14.1, Q10 (p. 215)

nodes.label: Problem Statement
nodes.description: A piggy bank contains hundred 50p coins, fifty ₹1 coins, twenty ₹2 coins and ten ₹5 coins. If it is equally likely that one of the coins will fall out when the bank is turned upside down, what is the probability that the coin (i) will be a 50p coin? (ii) will not be a ₹5 coin?
nodes.prompt: Read the problem. Answer each question to solve it step by step.
hints: Answer the question shown above the box.

nodes.label: What Is Given
nodes.description: 100 coins of 50p, 50 coins of ₹1, 20 coins of ₹2 and 10 coins of ₹5; each coin is equally likely to fall out.
nodes.prompt: What is given in the question?
accept: 100 coins of 50p, 50 coins of ₹1, 20 coins of ₹2 and 10 coins of ₹5
hints: How many kinds of coins are in the piggy bank?
Write how many coins there are of each kind.

nodes.label: What We Need to Find
nodes.description: (i) P(50p coin) and (ii) P(not a ₹5 coin).
nodes.prompt: What do we need to find?
accept: (i) P(50p coin) and (ii) P(not a ₹5 coin)
probability of a 50p coin and of not a ₹5 coin
hints: Read parts (i) and (ii) of the question.
There are two probabilities to find.
(i) a 50p coin, (ii) a coin that is not ₹5

nodes.label: Count All the Coins
nodes.prompt: How many coins are there in the piggy bank altogether?
hints: Add the number of coins of each kind.

nodes.label: (i) Probability of a 50p Coin
nodes.prompt: (i) What is the probability that the coin is a 50p coin?
hints: P(E) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes.
There are 100 coins of 50p out of 180 coins.

nodes.label: (ii) Choose a Method
nodes.prompt:
For part (ii), choose a method by answering either question:
Path A: How many coins are not ₹5 coins?
Path B: First find P(₹5 coin). What is it?
hints: Answer just one of the two questions.
Path A: which coins are not ₹5?
Path B: how many ₹5 coins are there out of 180?

nodes.label: Path A: Count the Coins That Are Not ₹5
nodes.prompt: (ii) How many coins are not ₹5 coins?
accept: count the coins that are not ₹5
nodes.jev_description: Count favourable outcomes for part (ii): coins that are not ₹5 = 100 + 50 + 20 = 170, P(not ₹5) = 170/180 = 17/18. Writing 170 identifies this path.

nodes.label: (ii) Coins That Are Not ₹5
nodes.prompt: (ii) How many coins are not ₹5 coins?

nodes.label: (ii) Probability of Not a ₹5 Coin
nodes.prompt: (ii) What is the probability that the coin is not a ₹5 coin?

nodes.label: Path B: Complement Rule P(not E) = 1 − P(E)
nodes.prompt: (ii) First find P(₹5 coin). What is it?
nodes.jev_description: Complement rule for part (ii): P(₹5) = 10/180 = 1/18, P(not ₹5) = 1 - 1/18 = 17/18. Writing 10/180, 1/18 or 1 - 1/18 identifies this path.

nodes.label: (ii) Probability of a ₹5 Coin
nodes.prompt: (ii) First find P(₹5 coin). What is it?

nodes.label: (ii) Use P(not E) = 1 − P(E)
nodes.prompt: (ii) Use P(not E) = 1 − P(E). What is P(not a ₹5 coin)?
hints: “Not ₹5” and “₹5” are complementary events, so their probabilities add up to 1.

edges.label: Path A: Count the Coins That Are Not ₹5
Path B: Complement Rule P(not E) = 1 − P(E)
